title: Samadhi: Meaning and Context
excerpt: Samadhi is a technical term for absorptive concentration in yoga and related literature. It is not a synonym for feeling calm.

quick_answer.question: What does Samadhi mean?
quick_answer.answer: Samadhi names absorptive states in yogic texts, especially late in the eight-limb path. Ordinary calm or focus is not automatically samadhi.

intro: Samadhi is absorption. In the Yoga Sutras it belongs with the culmination of practice, not with the first quiet minute.

sections.heading: What does Samadhi mean?
sections.content:
Commentators dispute the kinds of samadhi and what they know. The Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy keeps the argument visible. Buddhist traditions use related language with different metaphysics. Sharing a translation word is not sharing a doctrine.

The neighboring page is [yoga philosophy](/articles/what-is-yoga-philosophy/). Treat that link as part of the argument, not as decoration.

sections.heading: Where does the word come from?
sections.content:
Studios sometimes say samadhi for the rest at the end of class. That rest may be pleasant. The technical term is heavier. Meditation, in the same list, is a prior limb, not a synonym.

A wider map lives at the [yoga topic](/topics/yoga/). Dates and school names matter, because a recent American presentation is often described as if it had no date.

sections.heading: How is the word misused?
sections.content:
If you are a beginner, do not aim at the word. Aim at a clear cue. If you are reading, note which text and which commentator is defining the ladder.

If you want a narrower practical or comparative page, use [the yoga entry](/glossary/yoga/). You can understand the description without joining a group or buying a course.

sections.heading: What should a careful reader refuse?
sections.content:
Do not use samadhi as a boast or as a medical outcome. Do not assume a nap or a float tank is the state a sutra describes.

Readers in the United States often meet a simpler version of the same idea in a class, an app, or a short video. Name that simpler version instead of pretending it is the whole tradition. Traditional teaching, personal report, and research stay in separate sentences on this site. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) is the rule. The [disclaimer](/disclaimer/) applies whenever a sentence leans toward health, safety, or a promised transformation. The [corrections](/corrections/) page is how to challenge a factual mistake. Name the school, the text, or the century whenever a sentence would otherwise float free of history. A reader may stop at the definition when that is all the question required.

key_takeaways: Samadhi has a traditional job that popular English often widens.
Context decides which school is speaking.
This entry defines the word and points to a longer page.

faq.question: Is Samadhi a scientific term?
faq.answer: No. It is a term of yogic psychology and metaphysics, not a clinical score.

faq.question: Where is the longer page?
faq.answer: Read the philosophy explainer. The longer linked page carries the rest of the context.
